title: How to reduce lag on a 3d game setting using UNITY
author: OneMiners_Franzh
selftext: I just have this side project of mine it's like a zombie apocalypse survival game on a school setting it just a small scale map really, but in the middle of my development I was experiencing mild-high lag if I exported the game can you guys help me? Btw I am using free assets and modifying them on Blender, I am using Mixamo as well for the Npc's animations etc. I tried watching YT video but most of them are old vids. Thanks in advance guys appreciate it.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
What's causing the lag? Do you have high detail 3d models? Are you calculating something big every frame? Does the lag happen all the time or only at certain zones or events?

This is all Unity optimization and has nothing to do with AI. Although it's likely your use of AI has introduced unoptimized causes.

replies.author: OneMiners_Franzh
replies.body: I think it's the assets some of them are high detail especially the trees 😅

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: Start there. No excuse to have high res assets in a lagging game. Takes one hour to learn to lower poly count in blender.

replies.author: OneMiners_Franzh
replies.body: Yes I will, thank you for the advice 😊

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: Been exactly there on a AA project (not AI). Every time the camera spotted a specific asset (I think it was a car) the camera lagged. The team ignored it for months. I turned on wireframe view and noticed the engine in that car was extremely high poly count. It wasn't even visible except in one cutscene with the hood open. But it also wasn't culled properly so there was a performance drop whenever the camera looked at the hidden engine object.

replies.author: OneMiners_Franzh
replies.body: Whoaaaaa I see I see thanks for the insight on this one

replies.author: Super_Range45
replies.body: You probably should start with frustum culling, so you're not rendering things the camera can't see.

replies.author: OneMiners_Franzh
replies.body: That's an optional as well thanks 🔥
